structured_output.reasoning: users.py:9-11 builds the SQL with an f-string: `LIKE '%{name}%'`, with no escaping or validation, and runs it with conn.execute(query). get_user at line 5 uses a `?` placeholder, so the contrast is real. With name="' OR '1'='1" the query becomes `... LIKE '%' OR '1'='1%'`. SQLite parses `'1'='1%'` as false, so this exact payload may not return every row. `LIKE '%'` already matches every non-NULL name, though, so all users are returned anyway. A payload like `' OR 1=1--` or a UNION SELECT works unconditionally. An apostrophe in the input (O'Brien) breaks the literal and raises OperationalError.
